inspiration: Capped spawn pools: a pool has a maximum count and a spawn-state count; it refills one slot at a time when a member despawns. Pool members are either chance-weighted or equal-weighted (PoolManager.cpp lines 360, 372-386). This is the spawn-cap idea for row 23 (zone population), not any specific numbers.
Randomised respawn window: each spawn record has a minimum and a maximum respawn time and draws one at random on death (Creature.cpp line 60). Prevents a whole pack from returning at once.

Two timers per dead creature: a corpse timer that decays the body, and a respawn timer that waits until the corpse has gone and any linked-spawn check passes (Creature.cpp lines 818 and 901). Gives the death presentation a clear sequence.

Patch-windowed data rows: each pool template row carries a minimum and maximum patch and is selected by the current build (PoolManager.cpp line 685). Good model for zone and content rows that must be tagged by season or release.

The README sets a rule that custom behaviour sits behind a config option and is off by default, and that content lives in data rather than hard-coded scripts (README.md lines 21-23). Useful as a rule for our zone data.
Custom content as re-runnable SQL applied last (sql/custom/README.md line 2). A simple way to keep balance patches separate from base content.

Pools include game objects as well as creatures (PoolGroup<GameObject> in PoolManager.cpp), so nodes and chests can share a cap with monsters. Category-level idea for walk density (what appears every 20 s of walking).
Loot and spell content are plain data tables keyed by creature or ability (creature_loot_template, spell_template in sql/migrations). Category-level only: a per-creature material table with counts.

briefs.label: Capped roaming pack (zone spawn director)
briefs.why: A small pack that never exceeds a cap and refills one member at a time reads as a living population: you see a group, kill part of it, and the rest of the zone stays calm.
briefs.keep: a cap per pool; one slot refills at a time; members are a named group, not free spawns; respawn drawn from a window
briefs.change: our cap is zone data with a grace timer and a despawn when no player is near; packs stay at three attackers (our MAX_ATTACKERS ruling), and the cap is read from the zone file, not hard-coded

briefs.label: Patch-stamped zone row
briefs.why: Every row carries a minimum and maximum version and the server selects only rows that match the build. A content season can change a zone without rewriting the base data.
briefs.keep: version window on each row; selection by current build; base and override rows kept apart
briefs.change: our window is a season or release tag per zone, not a game build number; no copied rows

briefs.label: Corpse-then-return pair (death presentation)
briefs.why: A body that stays for a while and then a separate return timer gives the player a beat to loot or leave, and stops the same spot refilling at once.
briefs.keep: two timers: body decay, then respawn; respawn waits for the body to clear
briefs.change: our corpse is a loot ceremony with a short shaped decay and a fade, not a plain timer; the return is a zone-data value

briefs.label: Per-creature material table
briefs.why: One table that lists which materials a creature class drops, with counts, lets a designer tune a whole family of creatures in one place and makes the crafting input visible.
briefs.keep: one table keyed by creature class; item plus count per row; tuned as data
briefs.change: our class names, our material set and count ranges; add a rare tier roll; no copied rows
